reason: The narrative centers on Joseph, an enslaved/enslaved person of low social status, as the protagonist. The story follows his perspective through his work as a servant in Potiphar's household, his struggle with false accusation, his imprisonment, and his service to fellow prisoners (the cupbearer and baker). These are portrayed as ordinary people in subordinate positions. The narrative details Joseph's daily work, his responsibilities, his moral decisions, and his interactions with other non-ruling figures. While the text mentions powerful figures (Potiphar, Pharaoh's wife, Pharaoh), the story's focus and empathy remain centered on the experiences and perspective of Joseph and those in similar working/servant positions.
